key_insight: Strain controls how neighboring iodine vacancies reconfigure in CsPbI3, with compression favoring separation in some geometries and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping.
engineering_relevance: Strain and vacancy-pair orientation may offer design levers for managing defect migration relevant to perovskite solar-cell structural stability.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3.
Isotropic and biaxial strain comparisons of short-time vacancy hopping.
Static vacancy-interaction calculations using DFT and SevenNet-0.
evidence_signal: Trajectories show nonmonotonic strain-dependent hopping and orientation-specific responses to biaxial compression, while all examined static configurations exhibit repulsive vacancy interactions.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-level durability.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
